sources.metadata.WEBSITE-AOKI-SHORT-WIND: Impulse-based phase initialization for short windows. For either reconstruction algorithm, it can be enabled, disabled or selected automatically by window length.
sources.metadata.MODEL-M09-REPAIR80.refe: A spectrogram repair model trained for this project using the NAFNet method. It repairs the 80-band Mel spectrogram extracted from the GL waveform, then passes it to BigVGAN for synthesis.
sources.metadata.MODEL-M09-PARAMETERS.re: Trained for this project to predict window length and dynamic range from the spectrogram, duration and frequency calibration. NumPy inference is included and can also be used with basic GL.
sources.metadata.REF-BIGVGAN.reference_n: Used to synthesize waveforms from 80-band Mel spectrograms. This module uses the BigVGAN base 22.05 kHz pretrained model released by NVIDIA.
sources.metadata.REF-NAFNET.reference_no: The 80-band Mel repair model uses the NAFNet architecture with frequency, coverage and acoustic conditioning. This module uses repair weights trained for this project.
sources.metadata.REF-FAST-GRIFFINLIM.ref: Used for momentum-accelerated Griffin–Lim phase iteration. New application tasks use momentum 0.99. The website comparison uses identical parameters to demonstrate original GL (0), momentum GL (0.99), and the same momentum GL followed by Mel repair and BigVGAN.
sources.metadata.PKG-BIGVGAN-BASE.refere: An 80-band Mel vocoder released by NVIDIA, used in the full repair pipeline or for separate resynthesis after GL. CPU execution is supported, as is a CUDA Python environment that has passed the application check.

sources.metadata.SRC-ZAIWA.attribution: Adapted with permission from the MATLAB resynthesis code released by the team of 陆尧, 梁昌维 and 孔江平. We thank the three authors and the Linguistics Laboratory of Peking University for their support and permission.
sources.metadata.SRC-ZAIWA.adaptation_no: The original implementation is the MATLAB resynthesis code released by the authors. PhoneticToolbox adapts it to Python with permission, retaining the verified LPC inverse filtering, residual and pulse-continuum calculations; F0 can be extracted with Parselmouth / Praat. REAPER is an additional F0 option introduced by PhoneticToolbox for extracting creaky-voice F0. Version 3 adds explicit source and target selection, both directions, control-point editing and application, batch and task history, four-plot comparison and saving complete result groups.
sources.metadata.SRC-ZAIWA.adaptation_ca: PhoneticToolbox provides a Python implementation adapted with permission. To compare the original workflow and synthesis results, run the MATLAB code released by the authors and check the input materials and parameter settings.

sources.metadata.REF-M13-LEE-ZEE-2003.re: Corresponds to the Standard Chinese (Beijing) and narrow options. The bibliography has been verified; a character-by-character comparison between the broad/narrow columns and the paper remains to be checked.
sources.metadata.REF-M13-HU-1995.referen: Corresponds to the 胡裕树《现代汉语》 option. The verified revised 1995 edition (6th edition) is cited here; the historical character list did not record its edition or page numbers.
sources.metadata.REF-M13-HUANG-LIAO-2012: Corresponds to the 黄伯荣、廖序东《现代汉语》 option. The 2012 expanded 5th edition, volume 1, containing the phonetics chapter is cited here; the historical character list did not record its edition or page numbers.
sources.metadata.REF-M13-QIAN-1990.refer: Corresponds to the 钱乃荣《现代汉语》 option. The 1990 Higher Education Press edition is cited here. A revised 2001 edition from Jiangsu Education Press is recorded separately; the historical character list did not record its edition or page numbers.
sources.metadata.REF-M13-WU-1992.referen: A phonetics reference added for the 吴宗济 option. The historical column recorded only the author name; whether this book and which pages were used remains unconfirmed.
sources.metadata.REF-M13-CHAO-1979.refer: Corresponds to the 赵元任《汉语口语语法》 option. The first 1979 edition of 吕叔湘’s translation is cited. The publisher product page describes a later reprint; the edition and pages used by the historical character list remain to be verified.
sources.metadata.REF-M13-FANGYIN-2003.re: Corresponds to the《汉语方音字汇》option. The reset second edition from 2003 is cited here; the edition and pages for the Beijing pronunciations used by the historical character list remain to be verified.
sources.metadata.REF-M13-UNTPHESOCA-2019: Corresponds to the UntPhesoca broad and narrow options. Based on the author website text accessed on 2026-10-11, with updates through 2024-10-11. Both columns use the middle variety as their baseline and select the first free variant. The third tone is 214 in broad transcription and 213 in narrow transcription. Automatic or manual erhua combination and individual splitting are supported.
sources.metadata.REF-M13-PINYIN-1958.ref: Corresponds to the Hanyu Pinyin option and provides a reference for letters, syllables and tone-mark placement. The scheme was approved on 1958-02-11; this module does not provide word-based orthographic segmentation.
sources.metadata.REF-M13-READING-REPAIRS: Used to check unusual readings and simplified/traditional character forms in the character list. Corrections apply to all conversion standards.
sources.metadata.REF-M15-R-QUANTILE-TYPE: Reaction-time quartiles use type 7 linear interpolation.
sources.metadata.M19-ZENODO.reference_no: Provides 930 survey sites, 510 linguistic features, MDS, clustering and five distance matrices. Cite both this dataset and the corresponding paper when using the data. Author names are retained as recorded on Zenodo.
sources.metadata.M19-PAPER.reference_not: The research basis for the dialect-similarity layer and distance schemes. Section 2.2 describes the coding of types, subtypes and co-occurring records. Original results are supplied in the accompanying Zenodo dataset.
sources.metadata.M19-SHAOZI.reference_no: Compiled county-level administrative-unit data used for dialect distribution. Original rows for dialect areas, dialect islands and merged tables are retained. Cite the dataset under its formal author name, Jing, Liwen, and state that it is based on the second edition of《中国语言地图集》.
sources.metadata.M19-ATLAS.reference_not: The original atlas source for linguistic phenomena: 205 phonetics maps, 203 vocabulary maps and 102 grammar maps, 510 maps in total. Map titles and category descriptions were checked against their legends.
sources.metadata.M19-LANGUAGE-ATLAS.refe: The atlas basis for county-level dialect classification, jointly compiled by two institutes of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the Language Information Sciences Research Centre of City University of Hong Kong. This module uses county-level data compiled from it by 井韶子 and published separately on Zenodo.
sources.metadata.M19-MCA.reference_note: Provides administrative-unit names, codes and parent relationships at county level and above for checking map-region correspondence.
